name: Cable branch joint
summary: A cable joint where a branch cable is taken off a main cable, drawn as a joint with a third cable leaving it.
description: A branch or tee joint connects a branch cable to a main cable without terminating the main cable at a switchboard. It is common on low voltage street mains and some legacy medium voltage networks, where services or spur cables are taken from the main along its route.

The symbol shows the topology but not the protection of the branch. A branch made by a joint generally has no switching or fault isolation at the tee, so faults on the branch affect the main circuit's protection. Readers should check protection grading and fault level at the branch cable.
readingNotes: Check how the branch is protected, since there may be no device at the joint.
Record joint location for fault finding.
drawingChecklist: Show the branch cable size and type.
Locate the joint on the route drawing.
distinction: A branch joint connects a third cable mid-route; a one-line bus tap is a connection to a busbar, not a cable.
